doc.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012

title: Charts students should study
summary: He recommends Schneider's Hang Gliding, Gil Evans and Brookmeyer.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I can tell. Can you name three charts, off the top of your head, that you definitely want your writing students to listen to and analyze?

That’s a good question. Let’s see. “Hang Gliding” by Maria Schneider would be one, which is one of her masterpieces I think; and probably anything by Gil Evans, I mean you can’t go wrong there; and then I have so many favorites of Brookmeyer’s so I guess something of Bob’s. I could be more specific if I really was prepared to think about it, but I would say those — but “Hang Gliding” by Maria Schneider for sure, and then Gil Evans and Bob Brookmeyer. I think if you really dig into those you’d have quite a bit of fuel to go into your future for a while.
